the ask, verbatim
Produce ONE test edition of Open Interest's daily crypto-discourse brief through the paper's full pipeline: three independent drafts, one selection, one adversarial review. The edition spec that every draft must follow in full: Produce today's TEST EDITION of a daily crypto-discourse brief. Plain text only, under 900 words total. This is a drafting rehearsal: quality of voice and sourcing is the entire point. FIRST: fetch and obey the house style guide at https://raw.githubusercontent.com/openinterest-ai/paper/main/style-guide.html Its rules are binding: declarative sentences, numbers with context, no banned words (delve, landscape, game-changer, seamless, robust, unlock, tapestry, paradigm, "it's worth noting", "ever-evolving", emoji), at most one em dash in the whole edition, absolute dates only, no financial advice. SOURCES: open platforms only (Farcaster, research blogs, Mirror, Substack, governance forums, GitHub; X only via open mirrors). Prefer the last 24-48 hours. A claim that cannot be verified against an open-platform source is cut, and the cut is noted in METHOD. When sources conflict on a figure, prefer the primary source; otherwise state the range and attribute both. Cite with the full source URL in square brackets; for these plain-text test editions this overrides the style guide's numbered-citation example. STRUCTURE (exactly): LEAD: a headline (short declarative sentence ending in a full stop), a 2-sentence deck, then 150-250 words. Every factual claim carries a source URL in brackets. ALSO TODAY: exactly three items: category tag, one-sentence headline with full stop, 2-3 sentence summary, at least one source URL each. READING LIST: 3-5 links, each with a 1-line reason. METHOD: one closing paragraph: sources swept, hours covered, any items cut for failed verification and any claims resting on secondary sources. ACCEPTANCE: the structure above, complete; every claim sourced; under 900 words; no banned words; headlines are declarative sentences with full stops; absolute dates only (no 'this week', 'yesterday', 'the weekend'); at most one em dash in the whole edition. CONTINUITY: before drafting, fetch https://openinterest-ai.github.io/paper/rehearsal.html and the prior test editions linked there. Do NOT lead with a story a prior edition led with unless a material NEW development happened after that edition published; an ongoing story without a new development may appear only in ALSO TODAY, and only with the new angle stated.
